forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: Drought threatens planted seedlings at establishment: a review attributes increasing mortality of recently outplanted seedlings in dry regions to hotter and/or drier conditions intensifying planting stress, and reports high rates of seedling mortality on restoration sites in western North America [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_1, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_3]; novel levels of drought alone are attributed with causing complete restoration failure even when outplantings are used [ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_2].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: In Australia a dry spell at planting did not significantly affect sapling survival at four months, a mild event in the authors' own description [ev_drought_hazard_preece23_1]. All the remaining evidence is cited secondary statements from high-income or unspecified settings, the complete-failure claim comes from a perspective piece not specific to forests, and nothing left in this cell reports a survival or mortality rate for the setting it describes. The Spanish dryland project whose mortality tracked a drought index has moved to the plantation family's drought row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: The compiler for dune stabilisation and afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan judges it to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating, not a measurement of storm damage to plantings, from a desert dune setting in an upper-middle-income country outside the low-income target [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm]. The Uganda tree-planting rating sits in the plantation family's row. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: A review of reforestation in tropical developing countries, citing an earlier study second-hand, lists uncontrolled fires, together with uncontrolled grazing, weed competition and cutting for fuel, fodder, poles and lumber, among the main causes of reforestation failure [ev_fire_hazard_le12_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: one second-hand narrative statement that does not separate fire from the non-climatic causes and does not quantify the damage [ev_fire_hazard_le12_1]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Australia, flooding rains that followed Cyclone Yasi flooded newly planted plots and drowned most saplings, and a perspective on restoration notes that a record drought followed by a year of heavy rain and flooding can cause high seedling mortality [ev_flood_hazard_preece23_1, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_3].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The compiler for floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan rates the technology as coping well with river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1509_2011_general_river_flood], so flood-adapted species and sites change the picture. The literature units are narrative from high-income or unspecified settings and the perspective piece is not specific to forests.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: Outplanted seedlings on open restoration sites are exposed to air at seedling height 10 °C hotter than at 2 m, with soil or litter surfaces up to 30 °C hotter, which causes heat stress, and even minutes of extreme heat can cause seedling mortality in many species [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_2, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is review-level and from western North America or unspecified settings, with the perspective piece not specific to forests; the microclimate effect arises after the overstorey is removed by harvest or fire.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for community protection of micro-basins through reforestation in Honduras judges it to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of landslide damage to planted stands [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Brazilian restinga, total mortality of planted seedlings over four years did not differ significantly between seasonally flooded depressions and dry sandbanks [ev_establishment_survival_loureiro21_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: This is a single site study in a sandy coastal plain, and both habitats had substantial mortality, so the null finding concerns the added effect of seasonal flooding only.

forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.mechanism: In Brazilian restinga, strong and constant wind causes branches to break and other damage to seedlings, directly affecting height growth [ev_climate_shock_loureiro21_1]. The Cabo Verde compiler judges afforestation as not coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1523_2011_local_windstorm].
forest_restoration__active_planting__ass.conditionality: Compilers for dune afforestation in Turkmenistan and reforestation in Honduras judge coping with windstorms or cyclones as good or moderate [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1529_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_extratropical_cyclone, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_tropical_storm]. The Brazilian statement cites earlier work and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements. The Spanish tree-shelter losses, the Vietnam smallholder-plantation typhoon evidence and the Uganda rating have moved to the plantation family's wind row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__bio.mechanism: Both directions are reported. On the gain side, planted stands create habitat and attract seed dispersers: beneath framework-species plantings in northern Thailand thirty-six tree seedling species recruited naturally, 25 of them animal-dispersed [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1], and WOCAT compilers rate dune afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan as raising plant, habitat and animal diversity, citing snakes, lizards and turtles [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_animal_diversity]. On the loss side, a pantropical review warns that where forests can regenerate naturally or with some assistance, tree planting can reduce biodiversity conservation benefits if the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__bio.conditionality: What separates the gain side from the loss side is what the land would do without planting. The cautions apply where forests can regenerate naturally and where the species or management chosen do not provide suitable habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_williams24_1]; the gains are on bare dunes and degraded tropical land with no unplanted control [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wydhayagarn09_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_1529_2012_plant_diversity]. The actionable reading is a siting and design choice: planting looks favourable where nothing would regenerate otherwise, and risky where natural regeneration is possible unless the species and management provide habitat. Both sides remain thin. The loss side is a single review warning, not a measured comparison; the gain side is compiler ratings and a case study without a control. The plantation-versus-natural-regeneration comparisons that used to weigh on the loss side have moved to the plantation family's biodiversity row, and so has the review finding that afforestation in north-west India mostly lost diversity and promoted monocultures; that family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up because plantation monocultures may not count as a nature-based solution.

forest_restoration__active_planting__car.mechanism: Planting native trees on former pasture in Brazil's Atlantic Forest built up carbon stocks of 21.85, 25.78 and 38.29 Mg/ha in successively older plantings, against 138.94 Mg/ha in mature forest [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_3]. WOCAT compilers rate above- or below-ground carbon as increased for dune afforestation in Turkmenistan and afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the Honduras compiler notes that the change in agrarian land use into forests reduces carbon and greenhouse gas emissions [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_750_2016_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. A review of nature-based solutions states that afforestation increases topsoil carbon in carbon-poor soils [ev_soil_organic_carbon_seddon21_5].
forest_restoration__active_planting__car.conditionality: The young Brazilian plantings held only 15.7 to 27.6% of reference-forest biomass [ev_carbon_sequestration_azevedo18_4]; that comparison with mature forest is held out of the class as a reference shortfall, but it shows how far young plantings remain from the baseline they restore toward. The same review marks where planting reverses the sign: the soil disturbance associated with afforestation causes significant losses in carbon-rich soils, especially of the deep soil carbon that takes many decades to accumulate [ev_soil_organic_carbon_seddon21_5]; afforestation on peaty soils can lead to losses of soil carbon that outweigh that sequestered as the trees grow [ev_carbon_sequestration_seddon21_7]. These are review sentences carrying cited findings rather than new measurements. Apart from the Brazilian stock measurements the evidence is compiler ratings, the Eritrea sheet combines planting with hillside terracing, and soil organic carbon enters this row as a component proxy. The pool now reflects restoration-toward-baseline planting: the afforestation soil-carbon meta-analysis, the planted-forest removal rates and the modelled plantation accumulation have moved to the plantation family's carbon row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cat.mechanism: Reviews of reforestation and afforestation find water yield falling. An FAO synthesis states that the effects of reforestation or afforestation on water yields are usually the reverse of those for forest removal, that low flows are usually diminished as well, especially where fast-growing, heavy water-using species are employed, and that water yield after maturation remains below previous values where grassland is reforested with Pinus or Eucalyptus [ev_water_yield_ham08_5, ev_water_yield_ham08_6, ev_water_yield_ham08_9]; planting forests on open land where the water table is close to the surface will lower groundwater levels [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_2]. A cited New Zealand study notes that afforestation can provide erosion reduction benefits while reducing water yield [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_4], and a global review warns that large-scale afforestation in water-limited environments will inevitably exacerbate water scarcity [ev_water_yield_zhang17_7]. The gain side is modelling: under full reforestation potential, water yield increased in 7 of 15 Asia-Pacific regions, significantly in four, by 11.4%, 16.9%, 17.6% and 84.9% [ev_water_regulation_teo22_1, ev_water_regulation_teo22_2, ev_water_regulation_teo22_3, ev_water_regulation_teo22_4], and spruce reforestation of a Heihe River headwater was predicted to increase annual runoff by 8.6% [ev_water_yield_zhang17_6].
forest_restoration__active_planting__cat.conditionality: What separates the sides is method and species. The losses are review statements about reforestation and afforestation in general and about programmes using fast-growing or heavy water-using species; the gains are model projections for large regional reforestation scenarios rather than project-scale planting, and the same model shows nonsignificant declines in other regions where heightened evapotranspiration outstrips increases in precipitation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_5]. The lowered water table under new forest is also described as improving drainage, so on waterlogged land it is not purely a loss [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_2]. The Pinus and Eucalyptus grassland result is a planted-forest case carried in the FAO synthesis; the measured paired-catchment losses after afforestation sit in the plantation family's catchment water yield row, which is parked out of the roll-up, so check that row before assuming that restoration planting avoids them. The review report that China's Grain-for-Green programme reduced water supply with mainly fast-growing non-native species has also been re-homed to the plantation family; without it the losses here are general review statements, and the row states no direction rather than a loss. This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: Tree planting and soil preparation are cited at US$1,400 to 34,000/ha across restoration initiatives [ev_project_cost_crouzeilles17_1]. In Brazil, direct seeding and seedling planting cost approximately ten times more (about US$2000/ha) than less intensive approaches, mostly due to the higher input costs [ev_project_cost_branc19_1]. Reported establishment costs run from restoring rain forest corridors by sourcing and planting trees in Madagascar to native-species reforestation in Chile and Colombia, reforestation in Costa Rica, eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil, and WOCAT afforestation sheets in Honduras, at US$5,402.39/ha, and Bosnia and Herzegovina, at US$6,078.79/ha [ev_project_cost_wri17_4, ev_project_cost_wri17_8, ev_project_cost_wri17_9, ev_project_cost_wri17_10, ev_project_cost_wri17_7, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_establishment].
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: The cost pool went thin with the split: the Mexican plantation-trial costs, the Madagascar plantation-establishment figure and the modelled plantation cost have moved to the plantation family's cost row, and the cost class here rests on the Honduras and Madagascar entries alone, the only ones in the low- and lower-middle-income band; the Brazilian survey figure is upper-middle income and stays out of that range [ev_project_cost_branc19_1]. Most figures carry no stated price year, the Brazil table entry mixes eucalyptus with native species, WOCAT costs are compiler-entered and converted from local-currency amounts, and the cited range spans restoration initiatives rather than a single project.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: The abatement cost of plantation reforestation combines implementation cost, the opportunity cost of land and carbon accumulated, net of revenue from selling harvested wood products, giving a modelled median of US$23.00 per tCO2 [ev_project_cost_busch24_4].
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: This is a single modelled estimate with a wide interdecile range, from US$-14.80 (plantations profitable without carbon payments) to US$724 per tCO2, so the figure is a screening value rather than a project budget, and it depends on wood-product revenue that a restoration (non-harvest) planting would not earn.

forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.mechanism: In a mulching experiment in tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, polyethylene mulch cut the cost of each established plant, including nursery costs, from 18.00 USD on bare soil to 2.45 USD, because 92 of 180 plants established against 10 of 180 without mulch [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. The saving comes from survival: the mulch costs money, but far more plants establish, so the cost per surviving plant falls.
forest_restoration__active_planting__cos.conditionality: Organic mulches lowered cost per established plant much less, to 12.50 USD with alfalfa straw and 13.33 USD with leaf litter [ev_project_cost_barajas13_1]. This row rests on one experiment at one tropical dry forest site, with costs in USD and no wider cost comparison, so the figures indicate the direction of the saving rather than a transferable value.

forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.mechanism: The only unit is a regional model of large-scale reforestation in water-insecure parts of the Asia-Pacific, in which extremely dry months became less likely in 9 of 15 regions [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: one modelled source at landscape scale, and most regional changes in the source's table were not significant and one basin moved in the adverse direction [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1]. It says nothing about plot-scale planting or measured drought impacts on rural livelihoods. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.mechanism: In a regional land-climate model, reforestation reduced the probability of extremely dry months in 9 of 15 Asia-Pacific regions, especially where it also increased total annual precipitation [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__dro.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single modelling study of reforestation at landscape scale, not observed project outcomes, and most regional changes were not significant [ev_drought_hazard_teo22_1]. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__fir.mechanism: The Uganda tree-planting compiler rates fire risk as unchanged, commenting that dense forest brings fire risk that is common in the neighbouring Kiruhura district but not yet a problem in Rubagano [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__active_planting__fir.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating, and its comment implies fire risk may rise as planted canopy closes rather than fall. No measured evidence on planting and fire is in the pool.

forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.mechanism: Catchment models in Slovakia and Luxembourg show reforestation and afforestation lowering flood peaks: in Slovakia a reforestation scenario cut a simulated peak from 84.8 to 74.9 m3/s and, for a 50% increase of forest, reduced peaks by about 24% on average, more for short storms than long ones, and an earlier scenario converting all arable land in a basin to forest cut peak flow by 42.3% [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. An FAO synthesis expects flash flooding to be reduced locally for frequent short, low-intensity storm events where soils are deep [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_7], and a global review states that afforestation in energy-limited environments will help to reduce flood risks [ev_flood_hazard_zhang17_1]. Compilers rate afforestation with hillside terracing in Eritrea, floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan, and afforestation in Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina as reducing downstream flooding or flood impacts [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.conditionality: What separates the benefit from the nulls is scale and storm size. The same FAO synthesis finds no evidence that reforesting watersheds reduces or prevents floods except at the very local scale of a few hundred hectares [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_5, ev_flood_hazard_ham08_6]; a Himalayan analysis concludes that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on local flooding, and certainly not on the Ganges and Brahmaputra mainstreams [ev_flood_hazard_ives87_1]; and a conference overview warns that reforestation in the mountains conceived as a palliative for the problems of the plains is likely to reap only disappointment [ev_flood_hazard_ivesmt87_1]. These are review and position statements rather than measurements. Much of the positive weight comes from high-income temperate catchment models at landscape scale, so transfer to low-income settings is weak, and the modelled benefit becomes less as rain continues [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3]. The largest figure is a secondary citation with no basin named [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. The remaining units are practitioner ratings: the Eritrea technology bundles planting with terracing, the Bosnia and Herzegovina compiler rates only a slight reduction, and the Honduras compiler rates no downstream change yet [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding]. No unit covers severe or extreme flood. For farmers the effect is off-site, arriving downstream of the planted land.

forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.mechanism: Adding forest to a catchment lowers flood peaks in models: in the Hornad watershed of Slovakia a reforestation scenario cut the simulated peak discharge by 12%, by 18% on average over the simulation period and by about 24% on average for synthetic storms, and a cited Alzette basin study in Luxembourg found an 8% reduction [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_1, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_2, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3, ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_5]. An FAO synthesis accepts that locally, for frequent short, low-intensity storm events, flash flooding should be reduced where soils are deep [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_7], and a cited synthesis expects afforestation in energy-limited environments to help reduce flood risks [ev_flood_hazard_zhang17_1]. WOCAT compilers rate flood impacts as reduced for Tugai floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan and for afforestation in Eritrea, Cabo Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_flood_impacts].
forest_restoration__active_planting__flo.conditionality: The flood benefit is off-site for farmers and local in scale. The same FAO synthesis finds no evidence that reforesting watersheds reduces or prevents floods except at the very local scale of a few hundred hectares [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_5, ev_flood_hazard_ham08_6]; Himalayan position papers judge that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on local flooding, and certainly not on the Ganges and Brahmaputra mainstreams [ev_flood_hazard_ives87_1], and that mountain reforestation as a palliative for the plains is likely to reap only disappointment [ev_flood_hazard_ivesmt87_1]. These nulls are expert positions, not measurements. The modelled effect shrinks for long storms (29% for the shortest rain duration, 17% for the longest) and the quantified evidence comes from models of large land-cover changes in high-income temperate basins, well beyond project scale [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_3]; the largest figure, 42.3% from converting all arable land to forest, is a secondary citation [ev_flood_hazard_bahremand06_4]. The Honduras compiler rates no effect yet, expecting flood reduction only in the long term [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_750_2016_downstream_flooding], and the low-income evidence is practitioner ratings, the Eritrea sheet combining planting with hillside terracing. The Uganda tree-planting rating has moved to the plantation family's flood row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__pro.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate afforestation as raising fodder supply, through cut-and-carry grass in Eritrea and through planted sand-fixing species used as forage in Turkmenistan, and also in Cabo Verde; the Turkmenistan sheet also rates animal production as increased [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1330_2010_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1529_2012_animal_production].
forest_restoration__active_planting__pro.conditionality: Every unit is a compiler rating rather than a measured yield, fodder is a component proxy for the production gap, and no unit reports crop yields; the Eritrea sheet combines planting with hillside terracing.

forest_restoration__active_planting__rec.mechanism: Recurrent costs are the annual maintenance of planted stands: compiler-entered maintenance for community microbasin reforestation in Honduras and for karst afforestation in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and a table entry of US$775/ha per year for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wri17_11].
forest_restoration__active_planting__rec.conditionality: WOCAT figures are converted from local-currency entries by compilers and the Brazil table states no price year; only the Honduras sheet falls in the low and lower-middle income band, so the recurrent-cost picture for poorer contexts rests on a single sheet.

forest_restoration__active_planting__rur.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate long-term returns on establishment and maintenance as positive or very positive for afforestation in Eritrea, Tajikistan, Cabo Verde, Turkmenistan, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Honduras, and the Eritrea compiler rates food security as improved [ev_food_security_wocat_1330_2010_food_security_selfsufficiency]. China's Sloping Land Conversion afforestation subsidies increased off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_iufro20_9], and the programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1].
forest_restoration__active_planting__rur.conditionality: Livelihood losses are documented: reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives [ev_household_income_le12_1], the Turkmenistan compiler reports income cut by 20 - 25% in the first 1-2 years [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income], and the Cabo Verde sheet notes that afforestation reduces the options of land use [ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Most positive units are compiler ratings, income, returns and food security are proxies for poverty, the Amazon returns are modelled for agroforestry restoration designs, and the Chinese ratio counts socioeconomic outcomes only and is cited in a systematic review [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]. The pool now reflects restoration-toward-baseline planting: the Vietnam smallholder-plantation returns, the Costa Rica reforestation payments to plantation owners and the modelled plantation profitability have moved to the plantation family's poverty row.

forest_restoration__active_planting__soi.mechanism: Planted cover reduces runoff and soil loss on the restored slope and catchment, so the benefit reaches farmers off-site, through less sediment and runoff arriving downslope and downstream rather than on the plot itself. In Pakistan a watershed restoration of tree planting, control of grazing and erosion control structures reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], and Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed areas with natural vegetation [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2]. A review of Chinese vegetation restoration finds it could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once vegetation cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1]. A model of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment finds that reforesting just 9.3% of it could cut sediment inputs from landslides by about 20% [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6], a Slovak catchment model shows reforestation decreasing surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1], and in Ethiopia tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff depth from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. WOCAT compilers in Eritrea, Cabo Verde, Tajikistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate soil loss as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1523_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4367_2019_soil_loss], with surface runoff and downstream siltation also rated as reduced [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1330_2010_surface_runoff, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4367_2019_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__active_planting__soi.conditionality: The Pakistan results are bundles - planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, check dams and spillways - so the reduction cannot be credited to planting alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2]. The Chinese evidence carries its own nulls: in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area vegetation and engineering measures together contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures in the past 20 years [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and a four-year measurement in 12 small Loess Plateau watersheds found an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover and attributed it to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1]. In New Zealand erosion benefits trade off against reduced water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]. The Waipaoa result is modelled and is landslide sediment recorded under erosion for lack of a landslide category, runoff and sediment enter as components, and the low-income evidence is compiler ratings apart from the Ethiopian runoff measurements [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. Plantation results, including the warnings that dense planted monocultures without understorey or litter can raise erosion, sit in the plantation family's erosion row, out of this row and the roll-up.

forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.mechanism: The Cabo Verde afforestation compiler rates downstream siltation as decreased, the sediment pathway to water quality [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating, and siltation is only a component of water quality; no unit measures water quality directly [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1523_2011_downstream_siltation]. The source is from an upper-middle-income country. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate water availability and the harvesting or collection of water as improved after afforestation in Cabo Verde and after afforestation of bare land in karst areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability].
forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.conditionality: The Honduras compiler for community protection of microbasins through reforestation rated water quantity unchanged, noting that effects of reforestation will show in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity], so expect any gain to lag planting. The pool is compiler ratings only, with no measured soil-moisture, spring or groundwater data. The downstream water cost of planting is not argued here; it is in the catchment water yield rows, and a loss there can sit alongside a local gain here.

forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.mechanism: The Uzbekistan compiler credits afforestation of degraded irrigated cropland with strong bio-drainage through tree transpiration [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__active_planting__wat.conditionality: The Uganda tree-planting compiler rates drainage unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_excess_water_drainage], so the strong rating rests on a single irrigated-cropland sheet. Both units are practitioner ratings.

forest_restoration__active_planting__win.mechanism: The Honduras compiler rates community reforestation of micro-basins as slightly reducing the impacts of cyclones and rain storms, explaining that forests reduce landslide risk, with a greater effect in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__active_planting__win.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single practitioner rating whose explanation works through landslide risk rather than wind, so it says little about protection from cyclone winds [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.mechanism: Drought kills planted seedlings during establishment: a review attributes rising mortality of recently outplanted seedlings in dry regions to hotter and drier conditions, and links high rates of seedling mortality at restoration sites in western North America to limiting conditions in the energy and hydrologic cycles [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_1, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_3]. Novel drought is credited with complete restoration failure even with outplanting [ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_2].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.conditionality: In Australia a short dry spell at planting did not significantly affect sapling survival, the soils having been saturated beforehand [ev_drought_hazard_preece23_1], so short dry spells at planting are not necessarily lethal. The evidence comes from high-income settings with none from low- or middle-income countries, the complete-failure claim is a perspective piece covering plant restoration generally rather than forests, and the review units cite other studies. Nothing in this cell reports a survival or mortality rate: the units describe raised seedling mortality in dry regions and on restoration sites without putting a figure on it [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_1, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_3]. The Spanish dryland reforestation losses are plantation results, reported in their own family rows, and no longer count toward forest restoration.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.mechanism: A review of hot, dry restoration sites in western North America links high seedling mortality to low soil water, high temperature and vapour-pressure deficit [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_3, ev_establishment_survival_gross26_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.conditionality: In Australia exposure of new plantings to a short dry spell did not significantly affect survival [ev_drought_hazard_preece23_1], so the threat depends on drought length and severity. The North American units are a review citing other studies. Plantation results are reported in their own family rows and no longer count toward forest restoration.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.mechanism: In Sri Lanka's dry and arid zones, mangrove seedlings and propagules planted in the higher intertidal suffered from drought and high irradiance, while those planted low in the intertidal of the wet zone were exposed to long submergence after heavy rains [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_2]. In tropical dry deciduous forest on Mexico's Jalisco coast, native-species plantings without mulch had low survival (5.5%), so the authors advise against planting without mulching [ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__drough.conditionality: Both units point to choices that change the loss: where in the tidal frame mangroves are planted, and whether plantings are mulched [ev_establishment_survival_kodikara17_2, ev_asset_drought_barajas13_1]. The row rests on two single field studies; neither measures drought intensity, and the Mexican survival figure does not separate drought from other causes of mortality.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__extrem.mechanism: WOCAT compilers judge planted and regenerating stands to cope well with local rainstorms: dune afforestation in the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan, area closure in Ethiopia, assisted natural regeneration in Niger and broadleaf plantations with assisted regeneration in India [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1529_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1598_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__extrem.conditionality: Thunderstorms are rated as coping well for the Indian plantations, while hailstorms are the only storm type rated as coping only moderately, for the same Indian broadleaf plantations [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm]. All units are WOCAT compiler ratings, not measurements, and none describes how storm damage to young trees would occur.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__fire.mechanism: Uncontrolled fire is listed among the main causes of reforestation failure in tropical developing countries, early-successional regenerating land that is not overseen faces a high probability of fire outbreaks particularly in dry years, and young regrowth forests fail to persist partly through vulnerability to fire [ev_fire_hazard_le12_1, ev_fire_hazard_chazdon16_1, ev_establishment_survival_williams24_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__fire.conditionality: These literature units are narrative and unquantified, and they list fire alongside grazing, weeds, cutting, market shifts and perverse policies. The only rated unit, from an Indian programme where villagers actively protect the forest, judges the technology as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire], which suggests the threat depends on whether fire protection is in place.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__flood.mechanism: Floods drown young plantings: in Australia flooding rains after Cyclone Yasi drowned most saplings in newly planted plots, and a drought year followed by flooding can cause high seedling mortality [ev_flood_hazard_preece23_1, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_3]. WOCAT compilers rate an Ethiopian area closure and assisted natural regeneration in Niger as not coping well with river floods, and the Khost learning site in Afghanistan as not coping well at all with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1598_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1626_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__flood.conditionality: The compiler for floodplain reafforestation in Tajikistan instead rates it as coping well with river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1509_2011_general_river_flood]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements and the literature units are narrative, so the severity of damage is not quantified; the floodplain system is rated more tolerant than the upland closure and regeneration sheets.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__heat_s.mechanism: On open restoration sites, outplanted seedlings sit in microsites where air at seedling height is 10 °C hotter than at 2 m and soil or litter surfaces up to 30 °C hotter, enough to cause heat stress, and even minutes of extreme heat can kill seedlings of many species [ev_establishment_survival_gross26_2, ev_establishment_survival_svejcar23_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__heat_s.conditionality: Both units are review or perspective statements citing other studies, from western North America or unspecified settings, and the perspective piece covers plant restoration generally rather than forests; no unit measures heat-driven mortality at a restoration site in a low-income country.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__landsl.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Bangladesh judges it not to cope well with landslides, and the compiler for broadleaf plantations and assisted tree regeneration in India rates it as coping moderately [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__landsl.conditionality: Community reforestation protecting microbasins in Honduras is judged to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_750_2016_landslide]. These are compiler ratings from a small set of technology sheets, not measurements, and none states how landslides damage the stands.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__sedime.mechanism: Rapid sedimentation and excess leaf litter can cause delayed mortality of mangrove trees by smothering their above-ground aerial roots [ev_establishment_survival_gijsman21_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__sedime.conditionality: This is a single review statement about existing mangrove forests, citing field and laboratory observations, not a measurement on restored stands, and it gives no magnitude.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__waterl.mechanism: In Brazilian restinga, total mortality of planted seedlings over four years did not differ significantly between depressions prone to seasonal flooding (53%) and dry sandbanks (46.5%) [ev_establishment_survival_loureiro21_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__waterl.conditionality: This single site study is the only evidence left in the cell, and it finds periodic waterlogging not necessarily harmful there; it does not quantify losses from longer submergence than the seasonal flooding of those depressions.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.mechanism: Wind damages young plantings: strong constant wind in Brazilian restinga breaks branches and damages seedlings [ev_climate_shock_loureiro21_1]. WOCAT compilers judge afforestation in Cabo Verde as not coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1523_2011_local_windstorm].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.conditionality: Most other compilers judge restoration technologies in Turkmenistan, Tunisia, Niger and Honduras as coping well with windstorms or extratropical cyclones, and reforestation in Honduras as coping moderately with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1529_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_750_2016_tropical_storm]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements. The Spanish shelter losses and Vietnamese typhoon damage to smallholder plantations are plantation results, reported in their own family rows, and no longer count toward forest restoration.

forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.mechanism: On a dryland reforestation project in Valencia, Spain, seedlings lost their tree shelters to windstorms and poor tethering [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1]. In Florida the 2005 Hurricane Wilma was estimated to have initially destroyed 1250 ha of mangroves, and frequent hurricanes have changed some mangrove ecosystems to mudflats [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1].
forest_restoration__asset_threat__wind_c.conditionality: The Spanish losses were partly due to poor tethering of shelters rather than wind alone [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1], and the Florida figure concerns existing mangroves and is a cited finding in a review, not a measurement on restored stands [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_marois15_1]. The row rests on two high-income studies, neither of which measures how damage scales with wind speed.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Niger judges it to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of storm damage to regenerating stands [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1626_2014_local_rainstorm]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The Niger compiler judges assisted natural regeneration as not coping well with general river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1626_2014_general_river_flood].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single practitioner judgement from a technology sheet, with no description of the damage and no measurement [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1626_2014_general_river_flood]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for assisted natural regeneration in Bangladesh judges it not to cope well with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet that gives no measure or description of the damage, so it is not a documented failure [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4372_2019_landslide]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Compilers in Niger judge assisted natural regeneration as coping well, or moderately on agro-pastoral and pastoral land, with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1626_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_2325_2017_local_windstorm].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: Both units are practitioner judgements from Niger with no description of the damage or measurement.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: Assisted regeneration recovers habitat by letting canopy cover and tree density build up: WOCAT compilers in Bangladesh rate animal and habitat diversity as increased as the habitat improved, and in Niger rate plant diversity as strongly increased where assisted natural regeneration is combined with planting selected species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_4372_2019_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_2325_2017_plant_diversity]. forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The low-income evidence is compiler ratings without species counts, and the measured evidence comes from a single restoration site in upper-middle-income Brazil using a specific nucleation technique, so transfer to other assisted-regeneration designs is assumed.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Niger rate assisted natural regeneration as raising above-ground biomass, especially on pastoral and sylvo-pastoral land, and report a rapid increase in soil organic matter; sheets from Niger and Bangladesh also rate soil organic matter as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_2325_2017_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_2325_2017_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_4372_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings with no measured carbon stocks or rates, and soil organic matter enters as a component proxy; the evidence is in context for low-income drylands and Bangladesh but has no measured backing in this row.

forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.mechanism: The costs are establishment costs per hectare entered by WOCAT compilers for assisted natural regeneration on agro-pastoral and pastoral land in Niger (US$90/ha) and in Bangladesh (US$197.62/ha), plus a table entry of US$639/ha for assisted natural regeneration in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_establishment, ev_project_cost_wri17_6]. A Brazilian cost survey groups assisted regeneration with natural regeneration and enrichment planting at about US$200/ha, roughly ten times cheaper than direct seeding and seedling planting [ev_project_cost_branc19_3].
forest_restoration__assisted_regeneratio.conditionality: The WOCAT values are converted by compilers from local-currency entries, the Brazil table gives no price year, and both Brazil entries are upper-middle income and so outside the low and lower-middle income range; the survey figure is a grouped value shared with other low-input approaches, not specific to assisted regeneration [ev_project_cost_branc19_3].
