In Tanzania, the compiler for riverine area enclosures rates bush-fire hazard as reduced, and attributes the reduction to the enclosure itself, fire breaks and local bylaws [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_fire_risk]. In Ethiopia, the compiler for an area closure on degraded land rates fire risk as slightly increased, without giving a reason [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: What separates the two ratings, as far as the sources say, is fire management: the Tanzanian reduction is credited to fire breaks and bylaws added to the enclosure, so it is a bundled result rather than the closure alone [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_fire_risk], while the Ethiopian closure names no such measures [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_fire_risk]. For scoping, pair a closure with fire breaks and enforced bylaws rather than relying on the closure alone. Neither side outweighs the other; both are single compiler ratings with no measured fire incidence, and the Ethiopian rating states no mechanism, so the idea that recovering vegetation adds fuel is an inference, not a finding. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Compilers judge that closing degraded hillsides and other degraded land in Ethiopia to let vegetation recover reduces downstream flooding, most rating the reduction strong and one noting that runoff from the watershed is highly reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from Ethiopian area-closure sheets, not measurements, so the row speaks to a single country and practice. One closure on degraded lands rates the downstream benefit only slight [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1598_2014_downstream_flooding].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for regeneration-based technologies in Ethiopia rate downstream flooding as reduced, one explaining that runoff from the treated watershed is highly reduced as vegetation recovers.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings from Ethiopian WOCAT sheets in a low-income setting, with no measured discharge or flood data, so the strength of the effect rests on practitioner judgement.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia report that regenerating enclosed areas mainly raise fodder production, harvested as cut-and-carry grass that in turn supports animal production; some also rate crop production as increased, citing deeper, more fertile soils and mulch made available from the area. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged, and the compiler-rated gains run mainly through fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield; apart from the Tigray study, all units are compiler ratings, not measurements. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Regenerating areas raise income through products sold or used from them: Ethiopian WOCAT compilers cite sales of grass and wood and better land productivity, and rate long-term returns against establishment and maintenance costs as positive or very positive, as do compilers in Tanzania and Tunisia. A forest-and-poverty assessment cites secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest improving farmer income in the coastal Atlantic Forest of Brazil, and a review notes that regenerating forests supply timber and non-timber products for local livelihoods.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The Tunisian compiler rates farm income as decreased and long-term maintenance returns as neutral, even while rating food self-sufficiency as improved. Almost all units are WOCAT compiler ratings, poverty is reached only through income, return and food-security proxies, and the literature units are cited examples or general review statements rather than measured income effects.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Recovering vegetation cover slows runoff and holds soil: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, attributing it to improved vegetation cover, controlled runoff and sediment deposited behind bunds, an Ethiopian compiler noting an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1607_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation]. A meta-analysis from Ethiopia finds areas closed for grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1], and in Leyte, Philippines, recovering forest on former slash-and-burn land generated the smallest share of overland flow among the land uses compared [ev_runoff_reduction_sidle06_1]. On harvested slopes, the higher probability of landslides following timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2], and a global forest-water assessment adds that land abandonment with expanding forest and grassland has in some cases decreased soil erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_5].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The same global assessment reports that abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes is particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4], and one Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as worse [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation]. Regrowth is slow to restore slope protection: young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support that its much larger and older predecessors did [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], and the landslide recovery result tracks regrowth after timber harvest, not a restoration project, without separating replanting from natural regeneration [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. Apart from these reviews and the Ethiopian meta-analysis, which measures runoff as a component of erosion, the units are compiler ratings, and some regeneration sheets combine enclosure with physical structures such as bunds, so the share due to regrowth alone is not isolated [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as less runoff and sediment downstream.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for regeneration-based technologies in Ethiopia and Tanzania rate downstream siltation as decreased, citing less sediment transported, improved vegetation cover with controlled erosion, and sediment trapped behind bunds; reduced sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as increased. All units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data, and some sheets combine enclosure with bunds.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate water quantity and the harvesting or collection of water as improved under area enclosure in Tanzania and area closure with Acacia reforestation in Tunisia, the Tanzanian compiler attributing it to a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: An Ethiopian compiler rates water quantity as unchanged under area closure on degraded lands [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity]. The pool is a handful of compiler ratings with no measured flow, soil-moisture or groundwater data. Water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: Compilers rate excess-water drainage in both directions. For one Ethiopian area closure and for closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia, drainage is rated as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage]; for another Ethiopian area closure it is rated as slightly worsened [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage]. None of the three ratings states a mechanism.
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: The sources give nothing that separates the two sides: no site, soil or design detail is attached to any rating. One visible difference is that the Tunisian technology includes planting acacia, whereas both Ethiopian ratings, one on each side, are for closure alone [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage]. All three are practitioner ratings with no measured drainage, so this row records a disagreement among compilers rather than a tested effect.

forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.mechanism: The compiler for an Ethiopian area closure rates wind velocity as strongly reduced as vegetation recovers on the closed land [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1414_2011_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__passive_regeneration.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating of everyday wind speed; it says nothing about cyclone or storm damage to people or to the regenerating stand.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: On a Mediterranean dryland reforestation project in Spain, the drought index correlated strongly with the course of plantation mortality (r = −0.72); about one quarter of the plantation was dead by the first year and more than half in the second, and the trend worsened in an exceptional, severe drought [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_1, ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: All three units come from one study in a high-income dryland, so agreement cannot be judged and the strength is not quantified. The authors add that an extreme drought can reveal, several years later, the impact of inappropriate technical measures that would otherwise remain concealed, so the losses mix drought with planting technique [ev_establishment_survival_delcampo21_3]. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda judges it to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1577_2013_local_rainstorm].
forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating, not a measurement of storm damage to plantings [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1577_2013_local_rainstorm]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.mechanism: In central Vietnam typhoon damage is a continuing concern for smallholder plantations and leads planters to favour short-cycle rotations [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1]; on a Spanish dryland reforestation project, windstorms blew away tree shelters [ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1].
forest_restoration__plantation__asset_th.conditionality: The Vietnam evaluation adds that the typhoon risk has so far not discouraged smallholders from continuing to plant, the Spanish losses were partly attributed to poor tethering, and the Uganda afforestation compiler judges the technology to cope well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_ieg18_1, ev_climate_shock_delcampo21_1, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1577_2013_local_windstorm]. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__biodiver.mechanism: The units that set the class point toward a biodiversity loss, but none states how large it is. A review of nature-based solutions states that if non-native tree plantations replace intact native ecosystems such as ancient grasslands, peatlands or woodlands, the outcomes for biodiversity will be poor [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_1]. On the Orissa coast of India, extensive Casuarina plantations established as a storm protection measure caused destruction to olive ridley sea turtle nesting beaches [ev_biodiversity_outcome_badola05_12]. The same review reports research in north-west India showing that although afforestation activities can lead to an aggregate increase in forest cover, in most cases they result in loss of diversity and promote monocultures [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_4]. Against this, the review allows a gain in a narrower case: establishing plantations of non-native trees in a highly degraded landscape might benefit biodiversity locally if the trees enable native vegetation to regenerate, or regionally if plantations take pressure off native biodiverse forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_2]. An INRAE expert synthesis's own small meta-analysis of species richness in plantations against natural regeneration of the stand after regeneration cutting finds no clear difference: -0.24, a very imprecise estimate from a very small number of cases, with an interval that spans zero [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1].
forest_restoration__plantation__biodiver.conditionality: The loss is stated without a size: the loss-side units are review statements and a cited case, none of which quantifies the decline against the land a plantation replaced, so the row reports a direction only and its strength is not quantified. What separates loss from gain is what the plantation replaces: intact native ecosystems, a nesting beach or a diverse cover replaced by monocultures on the loss side [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_badola05_12, ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_4], a highly degraded landscape where the trees help native vegetation return on the gain side [ev_biodiversity_outcome_seddon21_2]. The only quantified comparison against regeneration is non-significant [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_1]. Further INRAE statements point toward loss — plantations generally lead to decreases in biodiversity, or at least to changes in composition at the expense of native species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_6], and a cited 40% loss of local species richness in forest plantations relative to uncut control forest [ev_biodiversity_outcome_inrae23_2] — but they are held out of the class because their comparator is reference forest, not the starting point of a restoration project, so they describe a shortfall from a natural baseline rather than a restoration effect. The INRAE evidence is temperate and boreal, and only the Indian cases come from the low- and lower-middle-income target; the north-west India finding was re-homed to this family from active planting because it describes monoculture afforestation. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, because plantation monocultures may not count as a nature-based solution, and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__carbon_s.mechanism: A global review finds planted forests and woodlots have the highest CO2 removal rates, 4.5 to 40.7 t CO2/ha/yr during the first 20 years of growth [ev_carbon_sequestration_bernal18_1], and plantation reforestation with cyclical harvest accumulates a modelled median of 44.6 tC/ha across aboveground and belowground biomass, soil and harvested wood products [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. Soil carbon also rises: afforestation of cropland raised soil organic carbon stocks by 26% on average and tropical transitions to plantation gained 0.919% of pre-transition soil carbon per year [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_busch19_2], and the compiler for afforestation of degraded irrigated cropland in Uzbekistan reports surface biomass growth of 20 t/hectare/year and soil organic matter up by 20% in the form of fallen leaves [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1533_2011_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_1533_2011_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
forest_restoration__plantation__carbon_s.conditionality: Soil gains are conditional: on pastures (3%) and natural grasslands the change was not significantly different from zero, boreal sites lost 1.5% while other zones gained 7 to 17%, low-clay soils showed no change, heavily disturbed site preparation cut the gain to 4% against 19% with low disturbance, and plantation density made no difference [ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_4, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_lagan09_10]; that meta-analysis draws mostly on high-income temperate sites. The planted-forest removal range spans eucalyptus, teak and pine among other species, and the modelled 44.6 tC/ha counts harvested wood products and is a discounted present value [ev_carbon_sequestration_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation results, planted forests, woodlots and plantations under cyclical harvest. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__catchmen.mechanism: Afforesting grasslands and shrublands reduced annual runoff on average by 44% and 31%, with proportionally larger reductions for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Cases in an FAO synthesis agree: the Fiji Pine Commission's planting of Caribbean Pinus in dry-zone grasslands resulted in dry-season streamflow reductions of 65 percent [ev_water_yield_ham08_7], and in South Africa, where nearly all plantations are on previously native grasslands, water reductions are in some cases experienced as soon as two years after planting, with maximum streamflow decreases relatively early in fast-growing stands [ev_water_yield_ham08_10]. A review of nature-based solutions reports that China's Grain-for-Green programme succeeded in rapidly increasing tree cover but used mainly fast-growing non-native species that have reduced water supply [ev_water_yield_seddon21_10], and adds that single-aged, low diversity, intensively managed plantations may reduce water availability in arid regions [ev_water_yield_seddon21_9].
forest_restoration__plantation__catchmen.conditionality: These are afforestation and plantation-forestry results, mostly from paired catchments and from grassland replaced by fast-growing exotic stands; the authors suggest the effects on water yield will be more severe in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_4], and in South Africa the maximum decreases occur early and then diminish [ev_water_yield_ham08_10]. Forest plantations of native tree species aged 25 to 45 years produce persistent dry-season streamflow deficits exceeding 50% relative to native old-growth forests, because of high water use by young, densely-spaced trees [ev_water_regulation_iufro18_3]; that comparison is against old-growth forest rather than the land the plantation replaced, so it is held out of the class as a reference shortfall. The Grain-for-Green result is a review sentence carrying cited findings, re-homed here from the restoration families because it describes planting of mainly fast-growing non-native species. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.mechanism: In a plantation trial on pasture in La Chontalpa, Tabasco, Mexico, semi-mechanised planting cost US$178/ha against US$217/ha by hand [ev_project_cost_keyes97_1, ev_project_cost_keyes97_2]; plantation establishment in the Masoala corridors of Madagascar is listed at 279 dollars per hectare [ev_project_cost_wri17_3]; and modelled implementation cost for plantations across low- and middle-income countries has a median of US$3,729/ha, inclusive of replanting after harvest cycles, against US$140/ha for natural regeneration [ev_project_cost_busch24_2].
forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.conditionality: The cost class is set by the Madagascar entry, the only one in the low-income band; the Mexican and modelled figures sit outside it. The Mexican figures are historical field costs for establishment and first-year maintenance that exclude donated seedlings, and the modelled median counts replanting over harvest cycles, with an interdecile range of US$1,530–11,675/ha [ev_project_cost_busch24_2]. These are production-plantation costs, not the cost of restoration toward a natural baseline. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.mechanism: Modelled across areas feasible for plantation in low- and middle-income countries, the abatement cost of climate mitigation through plantation, accounting for revenue from the sale of harvested wood products, has a median of US$23.00 per tCO2, with an interdecile range of US$−14.80 to 724 [ev_project_cost_busch24_4].
forest_restoration__plantation__cost_per.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a cost class: one modelled source, and the figure nets out wood-product revenue, which is why its range reaches below zero [ev_project_cost_busch24_4]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__fire__al.mechanism: A review of nature-based solutions warns that afforestation of fire-adapted savannah and dryland grassland risks much greater carbon losses during intensely hot plantation fires, whereas those ecosystems readily recover from the relatively cool and frequent grassland fires, and that afforestation can also increase the risk of fires on peatland in temperate regions [ev_fire_hazard_seddon21_8]. The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates fire risk as unchanged so far, but notes that with dense forest comes the risk of fire, which is common in a neighbouring district though not yet a problem locally [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk].
forest_restoration__plantation__fire__al.conditionality: The worsening direction rests on a review sentence that carries the finding from the studies it cites rather than measuring fire itself, and it is aimed at afforestation that replaces fire-adapted open ecosystems or peatland [ev_fire_hazard_seddon21_8]. The Uganda unit is a null rating with a warning attached, not a measured change [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_fire_risk]. Neither unit gives a size, and neither comes from a measured fire record. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations and afforestation, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__flood__a.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates downstream flooding as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__plantation__flood__a.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, a judgement rather than a measured flood record [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__flood_ha.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates downstream flooding as reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding].
forest_restoration__plantation__flood_ha.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measured flood record [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_flooding]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__rural_po.mechanism: In Vietnam smallholder plantations were a sound investment, with an economic rate of return of 13.2 percent at completion and substantial financial gains for participants, mainly because low-interest loans reduced up-front costs to near zero [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_1]. In Guanacaste, Costa Rica, payments for environmental services under the reforestation modality made up 18.66% of participants' income during the contract, covered a substantial part of the costs of establishing and maintaining the plantation, and brought family employment and legal security over the property [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]; similar Latin American programmes reach around 10% of family income [ev_household_income_padilla17_2]. Modelled plantations would be profitable even without carbon payments across 28.3% of the area feasible for them [ev_economic_return_busch24_1], and compilers for afforestation in Uganda and Uzbekistan rate long-term returns as very positive, the Uzbek compiler noting that unprofitable land would start bringing benefit [ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income].
forest_restoration__plantation__rural_po.conditionality: These are production-plantation results: smallholder plantations, commercial plantations under a payment scheme, and modelled plantations with harvest. The Vietnam return fell short of the 17.0 percent expected at appraisal and the gains depended on subsidised loans [ev_economic_return_ieg18_1], the Costa Rica evidence comes from a high-income setting, and the Uganda compiler rates farm income as unchanged [ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income]. Most units are compiler ratings or modelled, and income and returns are proxies for poverty. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__soil_ero.mechanism: Under good tree cover erosion falls: in eucalyptus afforestation in Calabria, Italy, sediment concentrations were substantially greater on a plot with little or no tree cover, confirming the importance of the forest canopy in reducing erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1], and the Uganda afforestation compiler rates soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1577_2013_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation]. Erosion can still worsen, and this is reported as harm rather than averaged away: particularly serious erosion problems arise in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3], and an FAO synthesis names dense, planted monocultures with little or no understorey and ground cover as experiencing increased surface erosion rates [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_4].
forest_restoration__plantation__soil_ero.conditionality: Gains and losses both carry material weight, so no direction is stated. What separates them is the ground layer under the trees: the gains come where canopy and cover are good, the losses where understorey, vegetation and litter are absent, cleared or collected [ev_erosion_hazard_porto09_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_4]. The actionable reading is a management condition, keeping understorey and litter, rather than a property of plantations as such. Both loss statements come from syntheses rather than measurements and state no comparator; the gain side is a high-income Italian catchment study plus compiler ratings from Uganda. An earlier cited statement on throughfall energy under plantations without understorey was rejected at review for lacking a valid comparator and is not counted. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__water_qu.mechanism: The compiler for afforestation and tree planting in Uganda rates downstream siltation as decreased, the sediment pathway to water quality [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__plantation__water_qu.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating, and siltation is only a component of water quality; no unit measures water quality directly [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1577_2013_downstream_siltation]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up, so this row is reported as plantation evidence only and does not feed the restoration total.

forest_restoration__plantation__waterlog.mechanism: In Uzbekistan, the compiler for afforestation to rehabilitate degraded irrigated cropland rates excess-water drainage as improved at +3, through bio drainage through transpiration [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1533_2011_excess_water_drainage]; the Uganda afforestation compiler rates drainage as unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__plantation__waterlog.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets, not measured water tables, and the class rests on the Uzbek rating alone, for trees planted on waterlogged irrigated cropland. Whether the plantation family belongs in the forest-restoration roll-up at all is an open decision for the team, so read this row as plantation evidence, not as restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__plantation__wind_cyc.mechanism: A study of the Bhitarkanika mangroves reports, citing earlier work, that extensive Casuarina plantations established as a storm protection measure along the Orissa coast were ineffective in preventing damage, and that they caused destruction to olive ridley sea turtle nesting beaches [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_badola05_11].
forest_restoration__plantation__wind_cyc.conditionality: This row is data deficient: it rests on a single cited statement, not a measurement, so it is described here but does not set a class. It records a coastal plantation that failed as storm protection and harmed a nesting habitat; it says nothing about how much damage it failed to prevent. The plantation family is parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up and this row is published on its own: read it as evidence about plantations, not about restoration toward a natural baseline.

forest_restoration__production_gap.mechanism: Across restoration families the gain runs mostly through fodder and livestock: WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Tanzania, Tunisia, Niger, India, Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan rate fodder and animal production as increased, from cut-and-carry grass in enclosures, planted sand-fixing species used as forage and better grazing management. Crop gains are reported where regeneration improves soils or supplies mulch, and in Niger assisted natural regeneration in fields is reported to raise millet and sorghum output by almost 50%; in Brazil the Reflorestar payments-for-ecosystem-services programme raised agricultural value added and production value in the poorest municipalities. In Tigray, Ethiopia, households downstream of exclosures harvested 188 to 222 kg/ha more than those beside open grazing areas in the drought-affected 2023 season, and a panel estimate put the grain advantage at 586.6 kg/ha [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_1, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_2].
forest_restoration__production_gap.conditionality: Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings, and one Ethiopian compiler rates crop production as unchanged; much of the evidence is fodder, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield. The Brazilian quasi-experimental gains apply to the poorest quarter of municipalities in an upper-middle-income state, and the source reports a heterogeneous, negative response in better-off municipalities. The Tigray advantage was concentrated in the drier year: no statistically significant yield difference was found in the second production year (2024/2025), and it concerns downstream cropland compared with open grazing [ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_3, ev_crop_yield_mezgebo26_4].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: For a bundled programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries under sustainable forest management in India, the WOCAT compiler judges the works to cope well with local rainstorms and thunderstorms but only moderately with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: all three ratings come from the same technology sheet, so they count as one source, and they are compiler judgements, not measurements of damage [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5243_2019_local_hailstorm]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The India compiler judges a village-protected programme of broadleaf plantations and assisted regeneration as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single practitioner judgement on a bundled programme, where coping is likely to reflect active protection by villagers rather than fire tolerance of the stands; it does not show the stands are undamaged by fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5243_2019_forest_fire]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The compiler for the Khost learning site in Afghanistan judges the technology as not coping well at all with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single practitioner judgement from a site that bundles several land and forest management practices, so the rating is not specific to forest protection, and it gives no description of the damage and no measurement [ev_asset_flood_wocat_7460_2024_flash_flood]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for a bundled programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries under sustainable forest management in India rates the works as coping moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__ass.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single compiler rating from a technology sheet, not a measurement of landslide damage [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5243_2019_landslide]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.mechanism: Protection and community forest management retain and expand forest habitat. GEF sustainable forest management projects show less deforestation than matched areas without projects [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management in Nepal reduced deforestation [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1], and forest cover increased by 8% under community management in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. A global analysis of community forests found environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate plant and animal diversity as increased under protection [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_5243_2019_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7460_2024_plant_diversity]. Forest governance instruments retain forest habitat: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]. World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation, regeneration of degraded forests and protection of biodiversity under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg13_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1], and in Bolivia four payment-like initiatives showed marked environmental protection effects, two intermediate and three weak [ev_biodiversity_outcome_robertson05_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__bio.conditionality: Most units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction, a component proxy for biodiversity, and the Mexican figure is a before-after comparison with no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. In south-west Madagascar transfers of management to communities were found superficial and unable to stop forest clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], and GEF project sites likely exposed to urban encroachment showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3]; the GEF evidence concerns existing forest under a bundle of protection and management rather than restoration. Governance effects are uneven: in the global community-forest analysis environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1]; under Van Panchayats the change in broadleaf crown cover was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], an evaluation of Vietnam's special-use forests found no clear-cut evidence that the project had a positive impact on biodiversity, noting that its tracking tool was not a suitable proxy [ev_biodiversity_outcome_ieg18_1], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. These governance units measure forest cover, deforestation or threat reduction rather than species, the Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in a systematic review, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__car.mechanism: Protecting and managing forest keeps carbon in place and lets biomass build up. GEF sustainable forest management sites sequester more carbon each year than their counterfactual and avoid deforestation [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_2], community forest management reduced deforestation in Nepal and increased forest cover in Puebla, Mexico [ev_landscape_forest_cover_iufro20_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1], environmental condition improved after community forest management in 56% of the 524 cases tracking it in a global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], and WOCAT compilers for community forests in Uttarakhand, India and for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rate biomass, soil carbon and carbon storage as increased [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_5243_2019_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_5243_2019_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7460_2024_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. Forest governance instruments keep carbon in standing forest by retaining cover: a meta-analysis of payments for environmental services found improved forest cover (SMD = 0.32, 95% CI [0.10, 0.55]) and reduced deforestation (SMD = −0.12) against comparison areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_snilstveit19_2]; community-managed Van Panchayats in India improved the annual forest cover change rate by 0.40 percentage points and decentralised administration of protected forests in Bolivia by 0.80 percentage points [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_3]; and World Bank evaluations report reduced deforestation and regeneration of degraded forests under participatory forest management, and a positive effect of payment schemes on deforestation in some countries [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_2, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__car.conditionality: Much of the evidence is forest-cover change used as a component proxy, and the GEF carbon estimate is derived from a model over existing forest rather than measured stocks [ev_carbon_sequestration_gefieo19_1]. Community management transfers in Madagascar did not halt clearing [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_1, ev_landscape_forest_cover_ramamo12_2], GEF sites under urban pressure showed negative outcomes [ev_landscape_forest_cover_gefieo19_3], environmental condition decreased in 32% of community-forest cases in the global analysis [ev_landscape_forest_cover_hajjar21_1], and the Mexican result has no counterfactual [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ceballos21_1]. Retention does not always show up as carbon: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on total forest carbon in community forests (SMD = 0.09) [ev_carbon_sequestration_snilstveit19_1], the change in broadleaf crown cover under Van Panchayats was insignificant (0.026 percentage points) [ev_landscape_forest_cover_samii14_2], and Bank-supported payment schemes were applied broadly rather than targeting high-value forest areas [ev_landscape_forest_cover_ieg13_1]. The Nepal, Indian and Bolivian estimates are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank statements report outcomes only where they were monitored.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cat.mechanism: Forests use more water than the land cover that replaces them, so standing forest passes less water downstream: as both natural and human-established forests use more water than most replacement land cover, even partial forest removal increases downstream water yields [ev_water_yield_ham08_1], and replacing forest cover with other land uses almost always results in increased runoff and streamflow [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_2]. All of almost 100 paired catchment experiments involving removal of forest cover gave higher streamflow totals [ev_water_yield_ham08_4]; first-year increases after clearance in the humid tropics range from 110 to 825 mm depending on local rainfall [ev_water_yield_ham08_3], the greatest percentage increase falls in the dry season [ev_water_yield_ham08_2], and daily late-summer flows rose by up to 300% after experimental harvest, though most daily changes were 50% or less [ev_water_yield_jon12_2]. Global syntheses agree: more forest cover loss tends to increase annual runoff in both large and small watersheds [ev_water_yield_zhang17_1], an increase in forest coverage reduces the share of rainfall leaving as runoff [ev_water_yield_zhou15_1], and changes to forests in water-limited watersheds can lead to larger water-yield responses [ev_water_yield_zhou15_2]. Harvesting or removing forest also raises groundwater levels [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cat.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks how much water leaves the catchment, not whether the restored land itself holds more, and it can coexist with the local gains recorded in the protection water stress row. Every unit compares existing forest with its harvest, clearance or loss, which is why the row sits in the protection family and not in the forest restoration roll-up; none measures the outcome of a protection or community forest management project. One measured result runs the other way: very small summer events decreased by more than 40% in the first 2 years after canopy removal in the Fox Creek basins [ev_water_yield_jon00_1]. The comparison of regenerating basins against uncut reference forest has left this row; it is carried in the cross-family row as a recovery shortfall that does not vote. The null stays named: 12 (of 61) large and 33 (of 252) small watersheds showed no significant change in annual runoff despite forest cover loss [ev_water_yield_zhang17_4]. The groundwater statement also cuts both ways: planting forests on open land where the water table is close to the surface will lower groundwater levels, improving drainage, while removal can move soil salts into the rooting zone [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ham08_1].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: Costs cover establishing community-managed forest and protection works: compiler-entered establishment costs on WOCAT sheets for an afforested community forest with plantation and fodder nursery in India and for a protected area in Afghanistan, and a WRI table entry for community management of forest resources with sustainable fuelwood production in Benin.
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.conditionality: The WOCAT figures are compiler entries, the Indian one converted from local currency and spread over mixed plantation and nursery areas, and the Benin figure comes from a project database with no price year; these packages include planting and infrastructure, so they are not the cost of protection alone.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: Two payment schemes report low programme costs per tonne of carbon: the PAS scheme in Brazil was estimated at 0.56 USD per ton of CO2, and the Ugandan scheme cost $0.57 per ton of delayed emissions against an estimated social benefit of $1.11 per ton, roughly two times the cost [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3]. A global spatial model estimates the break-even carbon price at which carbon payments would cover the land opportunity costs of conserving most remaining mangroves, avoiding release of their stored CO2 [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_2].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.conditionality: The Brazilian figure is a total programme cost given without assessing cost-effectiveness, and the Ugandan cost-benefit ratio is a simple calculation; both come from single schemes cited in a systematic review [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_2, ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_3]. The mangrove figure is a modelled break-even price, not a project cost, and is not specific to terrestrial community forest protection [ev_project_cost_jakovac20_2].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.mechanism: A systematic review of decentralised forest management reports, second-hand, that decentralised administration of Van Panchayat community forests in Uttarakhand, India is associated with costs approximately 1/13th of those under state administration [ev_project_cost_samii14_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__cos.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: one second-hand finding from one Indian state [ev_project_cost_samii14_1]. It compares the cost of administering existing forest, not the cost of restoring land, and gives no figure that transfers to another setting. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__dro.mechanism: Forest protection keeps the water regulation that standing tree cover provides. An FAO synthesis states that it is well established that partial or complete removal of the tree cover accelerates water discharge, increasing the risk of drought in the dry season [ev_drought_hazard_ham08_1]. In India, a programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries is credited with improved surface and subsurface hydrological functioning in the upper watershed, which increased springshed groundwater stores and enhanced stream and spring flows in the dry season [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_drought_impacts]. The compiler for a learning site promoting sustainable land and forest management in Khost, Afghanistan rates drought impacts as slightly decreased [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_drought_impacts].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__dro.conditionality: The FAO unit describes what existing forest does, framed as the cost of losing it; it enters this protection row through the existing-forest comparator, which routes such evidence to the protection family and keeps it out of the other families, and it is a review-level statement with no size attached [ev_drought_hazard_ham08_1]. The other units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets that bundle planting, regeneration and protection, so the effect cannot be attributed to protection or community management alone, and the Afghanistan compiler gives no reason for the rating [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_drought_impacts]. No unit covers severe or extreme drought. For farmers the benefit is off-site: it arrives as dry-season stream and spring flow downstream of a protected upper catchment, not on their own plots.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__dro.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate drought impacts as decreased; the Indian compiler attributes this to improved surface and subsurface hydrological functioning in the upper watershed catchment, which increased springshed groundwater stores and enhanced stream and spring flows in the dry season [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_drought_impacts]. An FAO review states it is well established that partial or complete removal of tree cover accelerates water discharge, increasing the risk of drought in the dry season [ev_drought_hazard_ham08_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__dro.conditionality: The WOCAT units are compiler ratings, not measured drought outcomes, and only the Indian sheet states a pathway; the Afghanistan compiler gives no reason [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_drought_impacts]. The FAO statement is about what existing forest does and what its removal costs, not the result of a protection or restoration project, which is why it counts in the protection family only [ev_drought_hazard_ham08_1]. The same review reports elsewhere that removal raises dry-season streamflow (see the protection catchment water yield row), so the dry-season direction is not settled within that source.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__fir.mechanism: The India compiler reports that villagers protect the intervention area from anthropogenic and wild fires, so the forest rehabilitated faster and has a lower risk of burning because of greener cover and less flammable pine-needle accumulation [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_fire_risk]. A World Bank evaluation of participatory forest management projects lists reduced incidence of fires among the environmental outcomes reported where those outcomes were monitored [ev_fire_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__fir.conditionality: The India unit is a single practitioner rating from a programme that bundles plantations, assisted regeneration and nurseries with protection, and the compiler adds that in pine forests needle build-up remains a major fuel source whose removal is a challenge for land users [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_fire_risk]. The World Bank evaluation reports the outcome as a narrative across projects, only where it was monitored, with no measure of how much fire incidence fell [ev_fire_hazard_ieg13_1].

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__flo.mechanism: This row describes the flood regulation that standing forest provides and that protection keeps; nearly all of it is evidence about existing forest, read through what happens when it is cut. In paired experimental basins in Oregon, a high-income setting, discharges in small basins increased by 50% in the first 5 years after clear-cutting and were 25 to 40% higher than pretreatment up to 25 years later, and forest harvesting with roads has increased peak discharges by as much as 50% in small basins and 100% in large basins over the past 50 years [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_2, ev_flood_hazard_jg96_3, ev_flood_hazard_jg96_1]. A later analysis of the same basins found large events increased by 25% at Andrews 1, 16% at Andrews 6 and 26% at Coyote 3 after 100% clear-cutting [ev_flood_hazard_jon00_1]. The same Oregon study separates the event types. Forest canopy removal accounted for significant increases (31–116%) in peak discharges during the first postharvest decade in 8 of 10 treated basins, but the affected events were small and fell in the fall (September–November), when soils are in moisture deficit, rather than in spring [ev_water_regulation_jon00_1]. Changes in snowpack dynamics accounted for significant increases (25–31%) in winter rain-on-snow events in four of five basins at the H. J. Andrews Experimental Forest [ev_water_regulation_jon00_6]. An FAO synthesis states that partial or complete removal of tree cover accelerates water discharge, increasing the risk of flood during the rainy season, and that for frequent rainfall events of short duration or low intensity forested soils may reduce or prevent flash floods locally [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_1, ev_flood_hazard_ham08_3]. At the local scale forests and forest soils reduce runoff through enhanced infiltration and storage, and peak flows rise after forest removal in small experimental catchments [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_2]. A country-level analysis of developing countries predicted that a further hypothetical 10% loss of natural forest cover would raise flood frequency by 3.5% to 28.1% and flood duration by 3.8% to 7.9% [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_1, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_2]; in Malaysia an analysis with adequate controls for confounding factors found flood risk increased after natural forest was converted to plantation crops and urban land [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_1]; and in Swiss valleys with more than 30% forest, snowmelt was more gradual and flooding risk lower [ev_flood_hazard_iufro18_2]. The WOCAT compiler for a protected learning site in Afghanistan rates flood impacts as decreased, with riverbanks revegetated [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__flo.conditionality: The harvest studies and the forest-loss analyses describe what existing forest does; they enter through the existing-forest comparator, which routes them to this protection family and keeps them out of the restoration families, so none of them is a restoration result. The Oregon large-basin increase is bundled with forest road construction and is stated as an upper bound, as much as [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_1]. The service fades with storm size and basin size. Complete clear-cutting without roads produced significant increases in fall and winter events but not for large events as a group [ev_flood_hazard_jg96_4], and at Andrews 10 large events did not change after 100% clear-cutting [ev_flood_hazard_jon00_2]. In the same study other types of winter events did not change, so only rain-on-snow peaks rose in winter [ev_water_regulation_jon00_7], and in the fog-prone basins changes in cloud water interception apparently offset changes in evapotranspiration in two partially cut basins [ev_water_regulation_jon00_5]. The fall increases came in small events (0.22- or 0.28-year return periods), not in large events [ev_water_regulation_jon00_1]. For the rarer prolonged or high-intensity storms, once the soil layer becomes saturated water will run off even where there is full, undisturbed forest cover [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_4]; forest soils reduce runoff only in small-scale rainfall events, which are not responsible for severe downstream flooding, and forests cannot stop catastrophic large-scale floods caused by severe meteorological events [ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_flood_hazard_faocifor05_2]; and small to medium peak flows are affected most while the largest events do not change noticeably [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_3]. At basin scale the link is not shown: the FAO synthesis cites a worldwide review of watershed research that found no cause and effect demonstrated between forest cutting in the headwaters and floods in the lower basin [ev_flood_hazard_ham08_2], studies in larger basins have not usually found changes after deforestation of up to 50% of the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_4], and a Himalayan analysis contends that on the Himalayan scale human influences, so far, are insignificant [ev_flood_hazard_ives87_2]. The cross-country analysis itself found little evidence that further forest loss changed flood deaths or damage [ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_3, ev_flood_hazard_bradshaw07_4], and a reanalysis found the correlation between forest cover or cover loss and flood frequency appears absent [ev_flood_hazard_vandijk09_1]. Read the class as a local, small-to-medium storm service, not a defence against severe or extreme floods. For farmers the effect is off-site, arriving downstream of the protected forest.

The Afghanistan unit is a practitioner rating from a learning site that bundles several land and forest management practices [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_flood_impacts]. Benefits fall downstream, off-site for farmers.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__pro.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings, and the gains are in fodder and livestock, a component of the production gap rather than crop yield; the Afghan gains coincide with grazing-management changes, so the effect of protection alone is not isolated.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rec.mechanism: Recurrent costs are compiler-entered annual maintenance costs per hectare on WOCAT sheets for the community forest package in India and the protected learning site in Afghanistan [ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance].
