forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rur.mechanism: Protection and community forest management can reduce poverty through forest income, employment and food from forests. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2], 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases (the underlying global review of community forest management counts 316 such cases) [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1], and community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards [ev_household_income_iufro20_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand and, in large studies controlling for socio-economic factors, drove poverty reduction [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1]: a meta-analysis of counterfactual studies finds small positive effects of protected areas on local monetary outcomes (g = 0.028) and poverty outcomes (g = 0.117) [ev_household_income_kandel22_1, ev_rural_poverty_kandel22_1], households in the Chitwan National Park buffer zone of Nepal have 19 percent higher per capita income [ev_household_income_kandel22_2], and across developing countries living within 10 km of protected areas with documented tourism lowers the likelihood of poverty by 16.1% and of child stunting by 13.4%, with poverty 8.8% lower near multiple-use protected areas even without tourism [ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_1, ev_food_security_naidoo19_1, ev_rural_poverty_naidoo19_2]. Exposure to standing forest feeds children: high forest exposure gives at least 25% greater dietary diversity in sub-Saharan Africa [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_1, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_2, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_3, ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_4], child dietary diversity rises with community tree cover across 21 African countries, and in Malawi children in communities that experienced deforestation had less diverse diets [ev_food_security_iufro15_2, ev_food_security_iufro15_1]. In a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent and by 66% for low-income households, consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management raised participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, poorer households compensated for lost land access gained 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. In Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1], households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_household_income_gefieo19_1], in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1], non-timber income rose after benefit-sharing at Bach Ma, Vietnam [ev_household_income_ieg18_3], and WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate food self-sufficiency and long-term returns as improved [ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_economic_return_wocat_5243_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__rur.conditionality: The pool is divided. The global community-forest review that reports income gains in 68% of cases also records 26% with no change and 6.3% with decreases, and it pools community with household income [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; the GEF forest-management portfolio has a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 [ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, local studies found no effect of REDD+ on material well-being, and an analysis in Indonesia found potentially negative effects [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6]; payment programmes have a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3], and payments had no significant effect on a food consumption index in Mexico [ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1], where the payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Benefits skew to the better-off: in Nepal poor and low-caste households receive much less while bearing more costs [ev_household_income_iufro20_3]; near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests forest income rose by an insignificant 2 per cent and lowest-quartile households lost 6 per cent and 10 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; at Bach Ma benefits were shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Livelihood components often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their livelihood aims, and benefit-sharing around Vietnam's special-use forests averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact [ev_household_income_ieg13_1, ev_household_income_ieg18_2]. Protected-area gains depend on tourism: no child growth or wealth gains were found near protected areas without documented tourism [ev_food_security_naidoo19_2], and the forest-diet effect turns significantly negative in richer communities [ev_food_security_rasolofoson18_5]. The protected-area, tree-cover and forest-exposure studies measure what living near standing forest provides, not the outcome of a restoration intervention; the Colombian benefit of $411–1,236 per hectare a year is a carbon valuation, not cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3]; and many figures are secondary citations in reviews or World Bank evaluation estimates without a comparison group.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.mechanism: This row describes the soil and slope protection that standing forest provides and that protection keeps. Forest cover provides the most effective barrier to natural erosion, and loss of forest cover to other land uses always increases human-accelerated erosion unless soil conservation is carried out [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]; in the Ethiopian highlands soil loss under forest averaged 1 tonne per hectare, the lowest of seven categories of land use [ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_3]. Land managers and scientists agree that forests lower the probability of shallow landslides, and to a lesser extent deep-seated movements, in upland areas [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_7]. Clearing removes that protection: in a US study area the number and acreage of slides increased four and one-half or more times after logging began in 1953, and the scarcity of slides on timbered slopes near logged areas strongly indicates increased susceptibility from logging [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_2]; investigations in steep forested terrain worldwide note up to a 10-fold increase in landslide erosion roughly 3–15 yr after timber harvesting, and rates of mass erosion can rise two- to more than ten-fold 3-15 years after harvest [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_4]; mean suspended sediment at managed Sabah catchments was several times higher in the most affected period after logging than before it [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_3]; and in Japan most landslides happened in young forest stands, shrublands and grasslands, the preventive function of the forest increasing with its age class [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_4]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis notes that landslips may occur due to the loss of forest cover, tree roots giving the soil mechanical support [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1]. WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, the Indian compiler noting that trees and other vegetation helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation], and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes reported by participatory forest management projects where monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__soi.conditionality: The role of forests for deep-seated landslides is considerably less, and during extreme events with copious rainfall, very weak slopes or seismic activity forest cover is unlikely to have any effect [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_8]; root support is limited to shallow (<1m) mass movements, and deep-seated (>3m) landslides are not noticeably influenced by forest cover [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_1, ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_2]. Nulls stay named: in Thailand landslide density appeared independent of vegetation cover, the storm magnitude overwhelming the stabilising influence of root strength [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_4]; a cited study found lumbering had no part in contributing to slide occurrence and suspected forest maturity of slightly raising slide probability [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_3]; and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The logging, harvest and land-use comparisons are evidence about what existing forest does and what its loss costs, not the outcome of a protection or community forestry programme, which is why they sit in this family and not in the restoration roll-up [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_1, ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_1, ev_erosion_hazard_ham08_2]. The India and Afghanistan units are compiler ratings from sheets that bundle several practices. Benefits fall largely off-site for farmers, as fewer slides and less sediment downslope and downstream.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: The Indian WOCAT compiler rates downstream siltation as decreased, commenting that the works helped slow down sediment and runoff [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single compiler rating of siltation, only a component of water quality, with no measured water-quality data; the rated technology is a bundled programme of plantations, assisted regeneration and nurseries under village protection [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.mechanism: WOCAT compilers in India and Afghanistan rate water quantity, availability and harvesting or collection as improved: the Indian compiler cites better soil water-holding capacity from slower runoff and improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, and the Afghan compiler cites water seeping into the ground through revegetation and improved land cover, recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water]. Peak-flow evidence from harvest experiments now sits in the flood rows, following the project ruling that peak-flow damping is flood mitigation, not water supply.
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__wat.conditionality: The compiler units come from sheets that bundle several practices — broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India, a learning site for sustainable land and forest management in Afghanistan — with no measured flow or groundwater data, so the gain cannot be credited to protection alone. They are practitioner ratings, not measurements. Benefits to farmers come from springs and groundwater fed by the protected land, off-site from the farm. Whether keeping forest standing changes the water passed downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.mechanism: The India compiler rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as strongly reduced, explaining that erosion from extreme rain storms is reduced by decreasing flow velocity [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__protection_cbfm__win.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state an effect: a single practitioner rating that describes rain-storm erosion, not wind damage. The rating is for a bundled programme of plantations, assisted regeneration and nurseries under village protection, so it cannot be credited to protection alone [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding.

forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.mechanism: Recurrent costs are annual maintenance costs per hectare entered on WOCAT sheets for regeneration, community forest and other restoration technologies in Niger, Bangladesh, India, Afghanistan, Honduras and Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_project_cost_wocat_2325_2017_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_5243_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_7460_2024_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_750_2016_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4367_2019_maintenance, ev_project_cost_wocat_4372_2019_maintenance], plus a WRI table entry for eucalyptus and native-species reforestation in Brazil [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]. A payment scheme in Costa Rica is estimated to spend between $255 and $382 per year per hectare of additional forest [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__recurrent_cost.conditionality: Values span a very wide range because the technologies and cost items differ, the WOCAT figures are compiler entries mostly converted from local currency, and the WRI figure has no price year [ev_project_cost_wri17_11]; the units from upper-middle-income countries were set aside from the class, which rests on the low- and lower-middle-income entries. The Costa Rican figure is a payment for keeping forest, expressed per hectare of forest that would not otherwise have been there, and is cited in a systematic review rather than drawn from programme accounts [ev_project_cost_snilstveit19_1].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty.mechanism: Restoration reaches poverty mainly through income from forest products, payments and employment. Restored forests contribute to diversified livelihoods and higher income from timber and non-timber products, naturally regenerating forests supply both, and secondary forest regeneration combined with palm-fruit harvest in Brazil's Atlantic forest improved farmer income [ev_household_income_iufro20_8, ev_household_income_chazdon16_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_10]. Community forest management in Nepal reduced both poverty and deforestation in an analysis of 18,000 community forests, 68% of community forestry cases reporting livelihood outcomes showed income increases (the underlying global review of community forest management counts 316 such cases) [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1], community forestry in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on living standards, and in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla community forestry provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]. In China, the Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, and afforestation subsidies raised off-farm labour earnings [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9]. Global modelling gives benefit-cost ratios of $7.5 to $30.9 for restoring 350 million hectares of degraded forest land and about $2 to $32 across forest biomes [ev_economic_return_wri17_1, ev_economic_return_wri17_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand, and households near GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. WOCAT compilers across Africa, Asia, Central Asia and Latin America mostly rate long-term returns as positive or very positive and food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved; the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least, and the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income]. Forest governance and payment programmes add measured income effects. A meta-analysis of payments for environmental services finds a positive effect on overall household income (SMD = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1]; in a systematic review of decentralised forest management, co-management raised regular forest income in Malawi by 26 per cent on average and by 66% for low-income households, per capita consumption expenditure in Ethiopian participatory forest management communities by 35 per cent, and forest income near Uganda's National Forestry Authority forests by 16 per cent [ev_household_income_samii14_1, ev_household_income_samii14_2, ev_household_income_samii14_3, ev_household_income_samii14_6]. World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually and in Honduras by 62 percent, and in Andhra Pradesh, India, 72 percent of wage jobs went to the poorest and poorer households compensated for lost land access gained an income increment of 40 percent [ev_household_income_ieg13_2, ev_household_income_ieg13_3, ev_household_income_ieg13_4]. Restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; China's Sloping Land Conversion programme had benefits exceeding costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]; and in Bolivia all the main groups selling environmental services improved economically [ev_household_income_robertson05_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty.conditionality: Negative and null findings are substantial. Even the global community-forest review behind the 68% figure records 26% of cases with no change in incomes and 6.3% with decreases, and it pools community with household income [ev_household_income_hajjar21_1]. Reforestation projects have often deprived people of food production and forest-product collection without viable alternatives, and restoration can reduce on-farm income by taking agricultural land [ev_household_income_le12_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_7]; the Turkmen compiler expects annual income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced, and the Cabo Verde compiler rates food security unchanged because the practice reduces land-use options [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable and the Gelose transfers did not raise community incomes [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]; REDD+ contributions in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, other REDD+ studies found no effect or potentially negative effects in Indonesia, and payment programmes have either a small positive or neutral effect on poverty [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_5, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_3]. Brazil's Reflorestar programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment, the GEF forest-management portfolio returns a benefit-cost ratio of 0.69 counting carbon only, and in Nepal benefits of community forestry go mostly to better-off households while poor households bear more of the costs [ev_economic_return_seixas24_1, ev_economic_return_gefieo19_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. Few studies have substantiated that services of restored forests alleviate poverty, and where they do it takes years or decades [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_4]. Much of the positive evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, carbon valuations rather than cash (such as $411–1,236 per hectare a year for forest conservation in Colombia), secondary citations, or subsidy-driven gains without a counterfactual (Wuqi) [ev_economic_return_wri17_3, ev_household_income_wri17_1], and protected areas, REDD+ and payment schemes are conservation instruments rather than restoration practices. The newer governance evidence carries its own nulls and losses: payments had no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11) or on a food consumption index in Mexico (0.09 SMD) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2, ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1]; forest income near Uganda's District Forestry Service forests rose by an insignificant 2 per cent, and households in the lowest income quartile saw forest incomes reduced by 6 per cent and 10 per cent, the gains being concentrated among wealthier households [ev_household_income_samii14_4, ev_household_income_samii14_5]; just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]; and around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. Mexico's payment scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2], and the Amazon returns are modelled. The decentralised-management and payment figures are cited in systematic reviews, and the World Bank income figures are evaluation estimates, the Andhra Pradesh one measured against project start-up rather than a comparison group. Plantation results, including Vietnam's smallholder plantations, Costa Rican payments for reforestation plantings and modelled plantation profitability, are reported in their own family rows and no longer count toward forest restoration.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In the high-income contexts the evidence is about payments for reforestation in north-west Costa Rica. Payments for environmental services represent 18.66% of participants' economy relative to their other income during the contract period, and the programme's overall economic impact scored 63.9%, mainly by covering a substantial part of the costs producers incur in establishing and maintaining the plantation, with family employment and legal security over the property the main perceived benefits [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: This is a small base from one survey of participants: the income share is a share of income during the contract, not a change against non-participants, and the impact score is a perception index rather than measured welfare [ev_household_income_padilla17_1, ev_household_income_padilla17_3]. The plantations are commercial reforestation under contract, so the gain rests on the payments, and the benefits declined for later contract cohorts as payments were not updated while labour and transaction costs rose. The mangrove cost comparison in this row is not a household benefit and does not set the direction: mangrove restoration projects reported a median cost of US$0.1 per square metre (range 0.05–6.43) and an average replacement cost ratio of 5 (95% CI 3.1–6.9) against breakwaters giving the same wave reduction, a saving in engineering cost that accrues to society [ev_frmg_nara16_3].

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: Restoration and community forest management reach poor households mainly through income, food and fodder. In a rigorous analysis of 18,000 community forests in Nepal, community forest management reduced both poverty and deforestation; community forest management in Madagascar had a small but positive impact on household living standards, particularly for those closer to forests and with more education; and household survey data around GEF forest-management sites in Uganda show positive income effects [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1]. The benefits of mangrove reforestation projects were found to outweigh their costs in the Philippines, and a World Bank study for coastal Bangladesh models livelihood benefits of mangrove restoration at 3,700 to 86,000 USD per hectare [ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. WOCAT compilers in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Honduras, India, Niger, Tajikistan, Tanzania, Uganda and Uzbekistan rate long-term returns on establishment and maintenance costs as positive or very positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1048_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1330_2010_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1533_2011_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1577_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1607_2014_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_7460_2024_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_750_2016_costbenefit_establishment_long], and most rate farm income, food self-sufficiency or production risk as improved: the Niger compiler estimates that assisted natural regeneration raises food security by 20% at least and reduces forage deficits so livestock keepers are not forced to sell their animals in the lean season, the Indian compiler cites more fodder and water, and the Ethiopian and Uzbek compilers cite sales of grass and wood and unprofitable land starting to bring benefit [ev_food_security_wocat_2325_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_5243_2019_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_wocat_1048_2011_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_1533_2011_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1330_2010_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1626_2014_risk_of_production_failure].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: Gains are uneven and sometimes absent. In south-west Madagascar conservation-oriented community management contracts were not profitable for lack of valid alternatives, and the Gelose transfers raised neither community incomes nor the money usable in the area [ev_economic_return_ramamo12_1, ev_household_income_ramamo12_1]. REDD+ contributions to household income in Nepal were nominal, from 3.2% of the poorest households' income to 0.3% for the less poor, and studies of community forest management in Nepal find poor and low caste households receive much less than well-off households while bearing more of the costs through patrol labour and grazing controls [ev_household_income_iufro20_4, ev_household_income_iufro20_3]. The Tunisian compiler rates farm income as reduced and maintenance returns as neutral, and the Ugandan compiler rates farm income as unchanged [ev_household_income_wocat_1568_2013_farm_income, ev_economic_return_wocat_1568_2013_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_household_income_wocat_1577_2013_farm_income]. Most units are WOCAT compiler judgements on technology sheets rather than household measurements; the Nepal, Madagascar living-standards and Philippines findings are secondary citations in reviews; the Uganda result compares household assets near and far from project sites; and the Bangladesh figures are modelled present values transferred from a global valuation meta-regression in grey literature [ev_rural_poverty_iufro20_2, ev_household_income_iufro20_2, ev_economic_return_hernmel17_1, ev_household_income_gefieo19_1, ev_economic_return_wbmang25_1]. Community forest management and REDD+ are forest governance instruments rather than restoration practices, and apart from the Nepal poverty analysis every unit measures income, returns or food security as a proxy for poverty.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: Payments for environmental services raise household income on average: a meta-analysis of payment programmes in low- and middle-income countries finds a positive effect on overall household income (standardised mean difference [SMD] = 0.25, 95% CI [0.09, 0.41]) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_1].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: The gain does not come from farming: the same meta-analysis finds no significant effect on income from agricultural sources (SMD = 0.11, 95% CI [−0.06, 0.29]), on income from nonagricultural sources (0.05 SMD) or on household assets (SMD = 0.04) [ev_household_income_snilstveit19_2]. Livelihood components of conservation projects often fail: just two out of 37 closed World Bank protected-area projects achieved their intended livelihood aims [ev_household_income_ieg13_1]. The row rests on a single systematic review with meta-analysis and a single portfolio evaluation; income is a proxy for poverty, and both concern payment and protection programmes for existing forest rather than restoration.

forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings income gains come from subsidies, payments and forest products. China's Sloping Land Conversion Program increased local incomes in Wuqi County by 164 percent and off-farm income by 20 times, afforestation subsidies increased off-farm labour earnings, and the programme's benefits exceeded its costs by a factor of 1.5 for socioeconomic outcomes [ev_household_income_wri17_1, ev_household_income_iufro20_9, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_1]. Community forestry in Mexico's Sierra Norte de Puebla provides year-round wage labour and a profit share of 10 to 20 thousand pesos per member after harvest [ev_household_income_ceballos21_1]; secondary forest regeneration coupled with palm-fruit harvest improved farmer income in Brazil's Atlantic forest [ev_household_income_iufro20_10]; restoration with agroforestry models in the Itacaiúnas basin of the Brazilian Amazon showed internal rates of return between 4% and 26% [ev_economic_return_nunes20_1]; World Bank support for participatory forest management increased participating household incomes in Albania by an estimated 30 percent annually [ev_household_income_ieg13_2]. Protected areas contributed to poverty alleviation in Costa Rica and Thailand [ev_rural_poverty_puri16_1], and WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde, Turkmenistan and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate long-term returns as positive [ev_economic_return_wocat_1523_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1529_2012_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_4367_2019_costbenefit_establishment_long].
forest_restoration__rural_poverty__incom.conditionality: Null and negative findings sit alongside the gains. The Turkmen compiler expects annual farm income to fall by 20 - 25% for the first 1-2 years, the Cape Verde compiler rates food security unchanged, REDD+ sites in Indonesia showed potentially negative effects on well-being, and Brazil's Reflorestar payments programme showed no statistically significant effect on municipal GDP or employment [ev_household_income_wocat_1529_2012_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1523_2011_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_household_income_iufro20_6, ev_economic_return_seixas24_1]. In Mexico payments had no significant effect on a food consumption index (0.09 SMD) and the PSAH scheme was less cost-effective than a protected area [ev_food_security_snilstveit19_1, ev_economic_return_snilstveit19_2]. Around Vietnam's special-use forests benefit-sharing averaged US$1,053 per community, too small to have any discernible impact on livelihoods, while at Bach Ma non-timber income rose but was shared unevenly and two-thirds of product types were over-harvested [ev_household_income_ieg18_2, ev_household_income_ieg18_3]. The Chinese gains are subsidy-driven and the Wuqi figure has no counterfactual, the Colombian figure is a carbon valuation rather than cash income [ev_economic_return_wri17_3], the Amazon returns are modelled, and the payment and benefit-cost figures are cited in systematic reviews. Plantation results, including Vietnam's smallholder plantations and Latin American payments for reforestation plantings, are reported in their own family rows and no longer count toward forest restoration.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.mechanism: Tree cover reduces erosion by protecting the soil surface, slowing runoff and holding slopes, and the sub-practice rows agree on that direction. In the passive regeneration evidence, an Ethiopian meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and WOCAT compilers for area closures in Ethiopia, Tanzania and Tunisia rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased, an Ethiopian compiler noting an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years and less sediment transported [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_soil_loss]; the higher probability of landslides after timber removal diminishes substantially 15–25 yr after harvesting as replacement trees mature [ev_erosion_hazard_sidle06_2]. The planting evidence carries the measured and modelled magnitudes: in Pakistan a watershed restoration of tree planting, grazing control and erosion control structures reduced storm runoff and sediment yields by 55 and 78% [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_1, ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1], Chir pine planting with elimination of grazing at Balakot reduced surface runoff by 57% and sediment production by 69% against adjacent grazed land [ev_runoff_reduction_hanif90_2], tree planting on degraded Ethiopian catchments cut annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2], vegetation restoration in China could reduce soil erosion by at least 80% once cover exceeds 60% [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_1], and targeted reforestation of 9.3 percent of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment is modelled to decrease landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]. FAO syntheses call forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded cleared land, and in Taiwan a rehabilitation programme reduced reservoir sedimentation by 55 percent of the base rate [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. Community-managed sites add compiler ratings: the India compiler credits trees and other vegetation with mitigating displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands, the Afghanistan compiler rates surface runoff decreased, and a World Bank evaluation lists reduced soil erosion among the outcomes participatory forest management projects reported where they were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7460_2024_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. Assisted natural regeneration compilers in Niger and Bangladesh rate soil loss decreased [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk.conditionality: The benefit is largely off-site for farmers: much of it is reduced runoff and sediment reaching downstream land and channels rather than better soil on their own plots [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. Nulls and dissent stay named. In China the soil conservation measures, including vegetation and engineering, contributed 12.1–13.9% sediment reduction in the Three-Gorge Reservoir Area, so the vegetation share should be less than 10% in most instances [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_2]; decreased Pearl River sediment loads had little to do with soil conservation measures [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_3]; and on the Loess Plateau an inversely decreasing trend of erosion reduction with vegetation cover was attributed to the immaturity of the planted species [ev_erosion_hazard_ran13_4]. A Himalayan position paper judges that reforestation will not likely have significant beneficial impact on soil loss [ev_erosion_hazard_ives87_1], young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support of its older predecessors [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5], abandoned land in previously terraced landscapes can be particularly prone to gully erosion and landslides, an Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_4, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation], and the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1]. The largest measured reductions are bundles: the Pakistan results combine planting with grazing control and, in the watershed study, check dams and other structures, and the Taiwan programme combines reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, so none can be credited to tree cover alone [ev_erosion_hazard_hanif90_1, ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. Many units are WOCAT compiler ratings, several sheets bundle closure or planting with structures such as bunds [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation], afforestation in New Zealand reduces erosion at the cost of water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3], and the runoff results measure a component of erosion risk rather than soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1]. Studies of what existing forest does, including logging and harvest landslide studies, sit in the protection family row and do not count here, and plantation results are kept in their own family row, out of this roll-up.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In high-income settings tree cover reduces erosion through slope reinforcement and slower runoff: reforestation of just 9.3 percent (159 km2) of New Zealand's Waipaoa catchment could decrease total landslide sediment inputs by about 20 percent [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6]; afforestation in New Zealand provides erosion reduction benefits [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3]; reforestation in Slovakia's Hornad watershed is modelled to decrease surface runoff [ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1]; and in Taiwan reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The New Zealand afforestation benefit comes with reduced water yield [ev_erosion_hazard_iufro18_3], the Waipaoa and Hornad results are model scenarios [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_bahremand06_1], and the Taiwan reduction is credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control and check dams, cited in an FAO review [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. A US observation runs the other way on slopes: young second-growth timber falls far short of providing the root support that its much larger and older predecessors did [ev_erosion_hazard_bishop64_5]. The row applies only to high-income contexts and does not transfer directly to low-income settings. Plantation results are kept in their own family rows, out of forest restoration.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings, planting, area closure and regeneration reduce runoff and the soil it carries. In the Potwar Upland of Pakistan runoff and sedimentation from sheet erosion fell 55 percent and 78 percent five years after tree planting and closure of slopes to grazing [ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5, ev_runoff_reduction_forbes11_1]; in Ethiopia, a meta-analysis finds areas closed to grazing and agriculture had runoff coefficients of 4% against 19% on control sites, and tree planting on degraded catchments reduced annual runoff from 242 to 148 mm/year [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. WOCAT compilers in Ethiopia, Eritrea, Uganda, Tanzania, Niger, Tunisia, India, Bangladesh, Tajikistan and Afghanistan rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as decreased [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1418_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1330_2010_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1577_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1607_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1626_2014_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_4372_2019_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7460_2024_soil_loss]: an Ethiopian compiler reports an initial 50% reduction in soil loss after 2–3 years, the Tanzanian compiler controlled soil erosion through vegetation cover, and the Indian compiler says trees and other vegetation helped mitigate displacement of soil from upstream areas to the lowlands [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1607_2014_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: An Ethiopian area-closure compiler rates downstream siltation as worse, and the Tajikistan compiler rates only a slight decrease in soil loss [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1509_2011_soil_loss]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements, some sheets bundle planting with structures (an Ethiopian compiler attributes reduced siltation to sediments deposited behind the bund), and the Pakistan result combines planting with grazing exclusion [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_erosion_hazard_forbes11_5]. The Ethiopian meta-analysis values are runoff coefficients and depths, a component of erosion risk rather than measured soil loss [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_1, ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_2]. One measured governance result is null: the REDD+ pilot in Nepal had an insignificant effect on signs of soil erosion in community forests (SMD = −0.15, 95% CI [−0.31, 0.02]) [ev_erosion_hazard_snilstveit19_1], cited in a systematic review.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: World Bank projects using participatory forest management reported reduced soil erosion among their environmental outcomes, where those outcomes were monitored [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. An FAO–CIFOR synthesis reports the opposite in a particular setting: particularly serious erosion in plantations where the soil has been cleared of vegetation and litter to reduce fire hazard, or where litter is collected for livestock bedding or fuel [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3].
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The two sources are separated by management of the ground layer, which is a design choice: the erosion problem is tied to stripping vegetation and litter beneath plantations [ev_erosion_hazard_faocifor05_3], whereas the reduction is reported for participatory management of forests [ev_erosion_hazard_ieg13_1]. For scoping, the sentence that matters is to keep understorey and litter in place; trees alone do not protect the soil. Neither side is strong: one is a portfolio evaluation narrative without magnitudes that covers only projects that monitored the outcome, with possible positive-reporting bias, and the other is a cited general statement about plantations; neither measures soil loss.

forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.mechanism: China's national reforestation and afforestation programmes increased forest cover with reduced soil erosion and sediment, and WOCAT compilers in Cape Verde and Bosnia and Herzegovina rate soil loss, runoff and downstream siltation as decreased.
forest_restoration__soil_erosion_risk__i.conditionality: The Chinese finding is a narrative summary of programme outcomes without an effect size, and the other units are compiler ratings; this row applies only to upper-middle-income contexts.

forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.mechanism: Lower sediment load is the component of water quality this row rests on. WOCAT compilers for planting, regeneration and protection technologies in Ethiopia, Tanzania, Cape Verde, India and Bangladesh rate downstream siltation as decreased, citing less sediment transported, sediment deposited behind bunds, improved vegetation cover and controlled erosion, and slower sediment and runoff [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1048_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1072_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1607_2014_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5243_2019_downstream_siltation]. An FAO forests-and-water synthesis calls forest restoration one of the best ways of reducing sedimentation in degraded areas of cleared land experiencing accelerated erosion [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_1], and cites Taiwan, where reservoir sedimentation from 1965 until 1985 was reduced by 55 percent of the base rate, attributed to a rehabilitation programme [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2].
forest_restoration__water_quality_risk.conditionality: One Ethiopian compiler rates downstream siltation as increased [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1418_2011_downstream_siltation]. Apart from the FAO synthesis, the units are compiler ratings of siltation used as a component proxy, with no measured water-quality data such as nutrients or turbidity, and some sheets combine vegetation with physical structures such as bunds. The Taiwan reduction is a high-income case credited to a bundled programme of reforestation with soil conservation on cultivated land, fire control, check dams, agroforestry and conservation farming, so it cannot be attributed to forest restoration alone [ev_sediment_retention_ham08_2]. The benefit falls off-site for farmers, on downstream water users and reservoirs.

forest_restoration__water_stress.mechanism: This row is about water on and under the restored land: springs, soil water and dry-season supply for the people who use them. Practitioners applying these technologies rate water quantity, availability and the harvesting of water as improved, one recording improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, another that the technologies improve the water-holding capacity of the soil by decreasing runoff velocity, another a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water, and another that through revegetation and improved land cover water seeps into the ground, recharging the water table [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability].
forest_restoration__water_stress.conditionality: Read this row as local supply. Measured groundwater-recharge evidence, which found recharge decreasing with forest cover expansion, sits in the catchment water yield rows; check wells and springs that depend on recharge there before assuming a gain. Timing matters: compilers in Honduras and Ethiopia rated water quantity unchanged, the Honduran compiler noting that effects of reforestation will show in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity]. All of the weight is practitioner rating from technology sheets, several of which bundle more than one practice, rather than measured flow or soil moisture. What restoration does to the water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings the positive evidence rests on infiltration and baseflow. In Ethiopia a meta-analysis found baseflow from catchments with exclosures 1.5 to 4 times greater than from cropland [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1], and a land-climate model projects a significant increase in water yield of 84.9% in the Irrawaddy basin under full reforestation [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. WOCAT compilers in India, Afghanistan, Tanzania, Tunisia and Niger rate water quantity, availability or harvesting as improved [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_5243_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7460_2024_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1607_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1568_2013_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1626_2014_harvesting_collection_of_water]: the Indian compiler says the technologies improve the water holding capacity of the soil by decreasing runoff velocity and cites improved spring discharge in the peak dry season, the Afghan compiler that through revegetation water seeps into the ground, recharging the water table, and the Tanzanian compiler a reduction in unproductive loss of both green and blue water.
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: Compilers for area closure in Ethiopia and reforestation in Honduras rate water quantity unchanged, the Honduras compiler expecting effects of reforestation only in the long term [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1598_2014_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_750_2016_water_quantity]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than flow measurements, several from sheets that bundle planting with other practices; the Ethiopian baseflow result compares exclosure catchments with cropland rather than with the degraded land before restoration [ev_water_regulation_meaza22_1]; and the Irrawaddy gain is a model projection at basin scale [ev_water_regulation_teo22_4]. This scope holds no measured catchment evidence of the water-yield losses that afforestation causes elsewhere.

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: A global synthesis of paired catchments found that afforestation reduced annual runoff on average by 44% when grasslands and 31% when shrublands were afforested, with proportional reductions even larger for low flow and losses of 62% at the driest grassland site, suggesting more severe effects in drier regions [ev_water_yield_farley05_1, ev_water_yield_farley05_2, ev_water_yield_farley05_3, ev_water_yield_farley05_4]. Trees use the water: tropical forest canopies commonly intercept up to 35 per cent of rainfall, which evaporates without reaching soil water reserves, and trees use much of the water that does soak in, so extensive reforestation or afforestation should not be expected to increase dry-season low flows [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: These results concern afforestation of grassland and shrubland in paired catchments, mostly in South Africa, Australia and New Zealand, rather than restoration of degraded forest land, so the size of the loss for restoring native forest on cleared land is not measured here [ev_water_yield_farley05_1]. The row rests on one global synthesis of measured catchments and one regional expert synthesis citing earlier work [ev_water_yield_faocifor05_1].

forest_restoration__water_stress__income.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate water availability and the harvesting or collection of water as improved after afforestation in Cabo Verde and after afforestation of bare land in karst areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1523_2011_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_4367_2019_water_availability].
forest_restoration__water_stress__income.conditionality: These are compiler ratings from two technology sheets, with no comment on how the gain arises and no measured flow, soil-moisture or groundwater data; the row applies to upper-middle-income contexts only. Water leaving the catchment for downstream users is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows.

forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.mechanism: Compilers for an Ethiopian area closure and for closure with acacia reforestation in Tunisia rate excess-water drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1568_2013_excess_water_drainage]. A different Ethiopian area closure is rated as slightly worsening drainage [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage].
forest_restoration__waterlogging__all.conditionality: The sources do not say what separates the two sides: the worsening rating and one of the improving ratings both come from Ethiopian area closures, and none of the three ratings states a mechanism [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1048_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1072_2011_excess_water_drainage]. All units are practitioner ratings, not measurements. The Uzbekistan and Uganda tree-planting sheets are plantation results, reported in their own family rows and parked out of the forest-restoration roll-up. Any effect would be off-site for farmers, arriving downstream or at landscape scale rather than on their plots.

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for broadleaf plantations with assisted tree regeneration in India and for community reforestation of microbasins in Honduras rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as decreased; the Indian compiler says erosion impacts from extreme rain storms are reduced by decreasing flow velocity, and the Honduran compiler that forests reduce the risk of landslides, with the effect greater in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings, not measurements, and neither comment concerns wind: they describe erosion and landslide risk under storm rainfall, so the row says little about shelter from cyclone winds or surge. The Honduras compiler rates only a slight reduction [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Compilers for mangrove afforestation in Bangladesh, a programme of broadleaf plantations, assisted tree regeneration and fodder nurseries in India, and community reforestation of micro-basins in Honduras rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced; the India compiler attributes this to lower flow velocity reducing erosion from extreme rain storms, and the Honduras compiler to forests reducing landslide risk [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5243_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets, not measurements, and none describes reduced wind damage: the explained ratings work through rain-storm erosion and landslides. The Bangladesh and Honduras compilers rate only a slight reduction, the Honduras compiler expecting a greater effect in the long term [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_4300_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_750_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.mechanism: Mangrove planting in northern Viet Nam is credited with protecting a sea dyke that a comparable typhoon had damaged before planting, and with cutting the share of shrimp-farm value destroyed from 90 to 25 per cent; planted mangroves in Hainan, China reduced mean wind speed behind the stand during typhoons [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_1, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_ifrc11_2, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_mcivor12_1]. Compilers rate mangrove buffers in the Philippines as reducing cyclone impacts and afforestation in Cabo Verde and saxaul dune belts in Turkmenistan as lowering wind speed, by 20-25% in the saxaul belts [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_578_2016_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1529_2012_wind_velocity].
forest_restoration__wind_cyclone__all__i.conditionality: The Viet Nam figures are uncontrolled before-and-after comparisons attributed to mangroves by the implementing Red Cross programme's evaluators. The Cabo Verde and Turkmenistan ratings concern everyday wind, not cyclones, and all WOCAT units are practitioner ratings.
